name: product_import
title: Import products into a store and confirm they landed
when_to_use: The user wants supplier products added to one of their stores and expects them to actually be there afterwards.

body:
# Import products into a store

Three calls. The first one only *starts* the work, so a chain that stops after it leaves the user believing products were added when nothing may have been.

## 1. `upload_products` — submit

Needs a store id (`list_stores_api` → `id`) and at least one product source in the body: `new_products`, `file_url` or `finder_categories`. The `asin` of a `new_products` entry is the supplier's own product id — the bare id or the full product URL, never a search or category page.

`status` in the body decides what is created: `1` (draft) leaves the products invisible to buyers until they are published; `2` (active) puts them on sale straight away. Ask which one is wanted if the user has not said — it is not recoverable by a later read, and the wrong choice is either an invisible catalogue or an unintended live listing.

The response is `{status, bulk_action}` and it arrives *before* the work happens. Keep `bulk_action.id`; it is the only handle on the job.

## 2. `get_bulk_action_items` — poll to a final state

Call it with that `bulk_action_id` and the same `store_ids`. Each item carries an integer status:

| status | meaning | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | created | keep polling |
| 2 | in progress | keep polling |
| 3 | finished | done, this item landed |
| 4 | canceled | it will not land; report it |
| 99 | error | it will not land; read the item's error and report it |

The job is over only when no item is left at 1 or 2 — not when the call succeeds.

There is no push channel here, and every poll costs a turn, so the cadence is fixed rather than "as often as possible": wait **~10s** after `upload_products` before the first poll, then poll every **~15s**, and stop after **10 attempts** — about **~2.5 min** at that cadence. A tighter loop just re-reads the same unfinished job. If the ceiling arrives with items still at 1 or 2, say which items are unfinished and at what status — an import that is still running is a different answer from one that finished, and neither is "done".

A finished item carries the created product's id in `autods_product_id`; an item at 99 carries `error_reason` / `error_code`. A mixed result is normal and is *not* a failure of the call: some items reach 3 while others reach 99. Report both halves; do not resubmit the whole batch because one item failed.

## 3. `list_products` — confirm

Filter the store for what was submitted (by title, or by the `autods_product_id`s the poll reported) and check the products are present with the intended `product_status` and price. This is the step that turns "the job said finished" into "the user's store holds the products".

## When step 1 fails

A timeout or a server error on `upload_products` is **ambiguous**: the job may have started anyway, and nothing in the error says which. Retrying blind duplicates the listing.

1. The bulk id is lost, so step 2 cannot run. Look each submitted product up with `find_product_by_buy_id` instead: `buy_id` is the `asin` that was sent, as the bare supplier id (not a URL), one id per call, on the same `store_ids`. It answers `{status, id}` for a product the store holds, or `{}` for none yet.
2. `{}` is "not yet", not "failed": poll it at the same cadence as step 2 — ~10s, then every ~15s, 10 attempts.
3. A product comes back → the job started, or the store already held that product. Either way, do not resubmit it; continue from that `id`, at step 3 here.
4. Still `{}` at the ceiling → no product landed: the job did not start, or it failed. The submission may be repeated unchanged.
5. Confirm with the user before resubmitting: a duplicate listing costs them money to unwind.

An upload by `file_url` or `finder_categories` has no supplier id to look up. For those, read the store with `list_products`, filtered on the titles that were expected, at the `product_status` that was sent.

Use `find_product_by_buy_id` only here. When `upload_products` did return a `bulk_action.id`, step 2 is the route: it is the only one that reports an item that failed, and a failed item has no product, so a lookup by supplier id would read "not yet" until the ceiling.

`get_bulk_action_items`, `find_product_by_buy_id` and `list_products` are reads. A failed read changes nothing, so retry any of them freely.

## Done

`list_products` returns the submitted products, at the `product_status` and price the user asked for, and any item that ended at 4 or 99 has been reported rather than silently dropped.
